nodes.display_name: A to B Intake Cubicle Cross-Tie Flood Door
Weak configuration controls on flood door (physical, administrative, knowledge)
nodes.description: Inadequate physical, administrative, and knowledge-type controls governing the flood door's required closed position.

nodes.display_name: B intake bay cubicle layout limited personnel sensitivity to door condition
nodes.description: Physical layout of the 'B' intake bay cubicle limited personnel sensitivity to the abnormal open condition of the interconnecting flood door, compounded by inconsistent knowledge of door function, infrequent interaction, and operator rounds not highlighting door importance.

nodes.display_name: Procedural guidance omission on loss-of-safety-function during postulated REJ rupture
nodes.description: Available procedural guidance for opening interconnecting flood doors did not discuss the loss of safety function that would occur during the postulated REJ rupture when the door is open, contributing to delayed identification.

nodes.display_name: Interconnecting flood door left open/reopened after Feb 11, 2020 test
nodes.description: Door was verified closed after Feb 11, 2020 seal test but was subsequently reopened at an undetermined time; discovered open on Sept 16, 2020.

nodes.display_name: Both trains of RPRW inoperable (common cause) for 218 days
Closed interconnecting flood door to correct position
Revised outside tour logs to include readings verifying both interconnecting flood doors SHUT
Updated training analysis forms for Unit 1 RPRW and Unit 2 SWS Initial Training Courses
Placed temporary stanchions and signage in front of interconnecting flood doors
Design and install locking mechanism at both interconnecting flood doors
Update Operations procedures to discuss impact of open flood doors in incorrect pump configuration
Change placards on interconnecting flood doors for clearer guidance
